claim: EU leaders at the special European Council in Brussels, which is due to end on Friday 27 November 2026, agree to provide Ukraine with €45bn of EU-borrowed financing for 2027 (the Commission's proposed loan), whether or not all 27 member states take part.

runs.scenario: Reuters and AFP report before the deadline, citing unnamed officials, that leaders have agreed to the €45bn, but Costa and the Council first confirm it publicly on Saturday. One reader could count the two reports as an in-window announcement under the media route; another could treat them as leaks and count Saturday as the first announcement.
runs.yes_requires: From 10:00 on 26 November through 23:59 on 27 November 2026, Brussels time, leaders must agree and announce that they will provide Ukraine at least €45bn in EU-borrowed financing for 2027, through the Commission proposal or a replacement they identify as serving the same purpose. Not all 27 member states need to participate. A decision in principle, a referral, or a smaller amount does not qualify

runs.scenario: Conclusions say leaders 'welcome and support' a roughly €45bn Ukraine facility covering 2026–27, only partly based on EU borrowing, and 'invite ministers to finalise swift adoption', while Costa calls it a political agreement and two wires say leaders 'backed the plan'. One reader treats this as the allowed endorse-and-call-for-swift-adoption path for at least €45bn of EU-borrowed 2027 financing; another treats it as principles only, a handoff to ministers, or less than €45bn of EU borrowing specifically for 2027.
